text:
maria: Quick sync — follow-ups from the GPU capacity postmortem. We promised owners/timelines for quota, scheduler tuning, and headroom planning. Can owners call out commitments here?

devin: I can take quota work. Plan: audit outstanding requests, reclaim unused reserved capacity, and submit quota increase request for prod by end of next week. ETA 2026-04-02.

lee: I'll own scheduler tuning (bin-packing + preempt policy). First step: reproduce spikes in perf lab and test new scoring plugin. Target PR for tuning config by 2026-03-31, canary rollout 2026-04-05.

priya: I'll handle headroom planning + runbook updates. Proposal: set conservative headroom target at 12% for peak+burst windows, add auto-bump policy for 30m sustained saturation. Draft runbook by 2026-03-29.

maria: Thanks. Can we add one short action each with an explicit success metric? Eg: quota -> "reduce queued jobs > 60s by 80% after reclaim/increase". Scheduler -> "tail latency p95 under 300ms for scheduling ops". Headroom -> "no capacity-triggered fallbacks in next 4 weeks".

devin: Agree. For quota I'll track queued jobs > 60s and orphan reservations. Success metric: queued >60s down 80% within 2 weeks of change.

lee: Scheduler metric: p99 scheduling latency down 50% vs baseline and p95 < 300ms on staging. Will post baseline numbers tomorrow.

priya: Headroom OK. Also want to add alert changes: split capacity alerts into (1) scheduler backlog and (2) node headroom low. I'll PR alert tweaks by 2026-03-27.

maria: Solid. Assigning owners in the incident tracker now. Small ask: include rollback criteria for each item. Eg for scheduler tuning: rollback if pod startup errors > 0.5% in canary.

lee: Noted — will add rollback gates to the canary plan.

devin: For quota change, rollback is simple: reassign reclaimed GPUs back and cancel the new request. I'll document steps.

priya: For headroom auto-bump, rollback = disable auto-bump + manual scale down if we see sustained underutilization for >24h.

maria: Great. Also noticed a recurring pattern in postmortems: several incidents mention "slow node replacement" after OOM or evict — that increases pressure on autoscaler. Can we add a small task to speed up node reprovisioning?

lee: Good catch. I'll add a follow-up: reduce node replacement time by tuning node-init and using faster image pipeline. Owner: lee infra-ops (me). ETA 2026-04-09.

devin: Another recurring item: quota requests sitting in cloud console for days. I'll follow up with cloud infra to set up a fast-path for urgent GPU quota changes. Target contact + process by 2026-03-30.

priya: I'll update the postmortem doc with these owners/metrics and link to the tracker. Will also schedule a 30-min follow-up sync one week after rollouts. Proposed: 2026-04-12 10:00 PT.

maria: Sounds good. ops-bot, can you create the incident-tracker ticket and calendar invite? Include owners and deadlines above.

ops-bot: Created ticket INC-2026-4321 with subtasks: quota-audit (devin), scheduler-tuning (lee), headroom-runbook (priya), node-reprovision (lee). Calendar invite sent for 2026-04-12 10:00 PT. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-4321

devin: I'll kick off the quota audit today and post initial numbers in this thread.

lee: I'll run the scheduler lab tests tonight, will upload logs to the tracker.

priya: Draft runbook in docs/incident/headroom-draft.md and will PR today.

maria: Thanks team. Quick check — any blockers we should escalate now?

devin: Blocker: need permission to reclaim some reserved capacity in org account. @maria can you approve?

maria: Approved. Please include a note in the ticket about which reservations changed.

lee: No blockers from infra side.

priya: No blockers.

maria: Perfect. We'll reconvene after the canary rollouts and quota changes. Marking action items in tracker as in-progress. :thumbsup:

(ops-bot: ticket INC-2026-4321 updated to in-progress)
